concepts.def: Music that blends features of different traditions - rhythms, instruments, scales and production - into a coherent new style.
Group whose track 'Release' fuses Irish Celtic folk, West African music and electronic dance production in layered grooves.
Esperanza Spalding's jazz performance of a Brazilian bossa nova song, featuring her voice with double bass and acoustic guitar.
West African instruments heard in Afro Celt music: the kora is a 21-string harp-lute, the talking drum bends pitch under the arm.
Gentle syncopated Brazilian groove derived from samba, supporting lyrical melody in an intimate, quiet texture.
Fusion producers combine loops, drones and live instruments in the studio, building textures gradually across a track.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Area of Study 4: Fusions — a core area of GCSE Music.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Area of Study 4: Fusions brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Area of Study 4: Fusions.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Afro Celt Sound System's music fuses which traditions?
options: Irish folk, West African music and electronic dance
Viennese waltz and opera
Gregorian chant and reggae
Country and gamelan

mcqs.q: On 'Samba Em Preludio', Esperanza Spalding sings while playing which instrument?
options: Double bass
Drum kit
Bagpipes
Trumpet

mcqs.q: The kora is best described as what?
options: A West African harp-lute with 21 strings
A Brazilian friction drum
An Irish whistle
An electronic sampler

mcqs.q: Bossa nova originated in which country?
options: Brazil
Ireland
Senegal
Spain

mcqs.q: Does fusion music mean one band simply covering songs from another genre?
options: No - fusion blends the actual musical ingredients of traditions, such as Celtic melodies over West African rhythms with dance production.
Fusion is just a rock band playing a reggae song.
Fusion means recording two albums at the same time.
Bossa nova is sung only by large choirs.
Bossa nova is sung only by large choirs.
No - the kora is a 21-string West African harp-lute, plucked to produce flowing melodic and harmonic patterns.
The kora is a brass horn played at festivals.
All traditional African instruments are drums, so the kora must be one.

mcqs.q: Is bossa nova fast, loud carnival music?
options: Fusion means recording two albums at the same time.
Bossa nova is sung only by large choirs.
No - bossa nova is gentle, quiet and intimate, with subtle syncopation, in contrast to the driving percussion of carnival samba.
All Brazilian music sounds like a loud carnival parade.
